explanation: `ZFNat` is the library's own type of von Neumann naturals. At line 1303 it has only `Zero`, `One`, `LT`/`LE`, `Preorder`, `LinearOrder`, `Add`, `Sub` and `Mul` instances, and its subtraction is the library's own `ZFNat.sub`. I searched the instance declarations in `Naturals.lean`: the `Semiring` and `CommSemiring` instances come later in the file, and I found no `OrderedSub` or ordered-semiring instance at all. So Mathlib's truncated-subtraction lemma `tsub_mul` cannot be applied in this setting. The result is right distributivity of the library's own multiplication over its own subtraction. All of its content lies in the library's definitions, and the proof only uses the library's own `left_distrib_mul_sub` and `mul_comm`.
